title: Cyclone Arnab: three dead in Kandhamal landslide, a dozen missing in Ganjam as Odisha floods spread
dek: More than 1,000 villages are under water in Ganjam and Gajapati and nearly 60,000 people have been evacuated. Andhra Pradesh puts its losses at Rs 4,600 crore, and another depression is due by Saturday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A landslide triggered by the remnants of Cyclone Arnab has killed three members of a family, including a nine-month-old baby, in Odisha's Kandhamal district, and at least 12 people are missing after a flash flood hit a village on the Ganjam-Kandhamal border, officials and local media reported on Friday, October 30. They are the first deaths reported in Odisha from the storm, which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast two days ago.

Floodwater has reached more than 1,000 villages across Ganjam and Gajapati districts, rivers in southern Odisha remain above danger marks, and close to 60,000 people have been moved to safety across nine districts. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi made an aerial survey of the two worst-hit districts on Friday.

## What happened

The Kandhamal landslide struck Dangesi village in Raikia block, news agency PTI reported. A young couple and their baby were killed; two other people were rescued and about 450 residents of the area have been evacuated. The Chief Minister announced ex gratia of Rs 4 lakh for the family of each person killed, and Panchayati Raj Minister Rabi Narayan Naik visited the site.

In Gidipabali village in the Bhanjanagar block of Ganjam, close to the Kandhamal border, a flash flood and landslide in the early hours of Wednesday swept through homes. OdishaBytes put the number of missing at 12 on Friday evening, while Ommcom News reported 13. Bhanjanagar Sub-Collector Umashankar Behera confirmed the incident and said a search was under way. Earlier reports on Thursday had said there were no deaths in Odisha; the missing figure is preliminary and may change.

Ganjam has been the worst affected district, Revenue Minister Suresh Pujari said. According to The Pioneer and Deccan Chronicle, 299 villages in 22 blocks of Ganjam and 711 villages in seven blocks of Gajapati have been flooded. About 2,000 people were stranded in Ganjam. Reports differ on the number evacuated in the district, from about 11,900 (The Pioneer) to 23,000 (ETV Bharat). The state government released an additional Rs 20 crore for Ganjam.

The Rushikulya river at Purushottampur was running at 19 metres on Friday morning, more than two metres above its danger level of 16.8 metres, The Pioneer reported, and it remained above the danger mark in the afternoon. The Bansadhara and Mahendratanaya rivers were also in spate. Floodwater from the Bahuda river reached the railway bridge near the Odisha-Andhra border, suspending trains, and submerged National Highway 16, where hundreds of vehicles have been stuck since Thursday. A stretch of NH-326 in Gajapati has been washed away.

Rainfall in the 24 hours to 8:30 am on Thursday was extreme in places: The Pioneer recorded 546 mm at Patrapur and 503 mm at Sorada in Ganjam, though other outlets, quoting the state's Engineer-in-Chief, gave lower figures for both.

## In Andhra Pradesh

Andhra Pradesh, where Arnab made landfall early on Wednesday as a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of up to 135 km/h, has put its preliminary losses at about Rs 4,600 crore, a figure Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has said could rise. The state government's count of deaths stands at seven, though some outlets have reported up to nine. About 2.24 lakh hectares of crops across 14 districts were damaged, affecting about 3.45 lakh farmers, according to The Pioneer; West Godavari, Konaseema and Kakinada were the hardest hit. Damage to the power network alone has been estimated at Rs 500 crore, with at least 15,000 electricity poles down.

In Srikakulam district, on the border with Odisha, about 10,000 people were in relief camps at Ichchapuram, NewsBytes reported.

## Background

Arnab crossed the Andhra coast on October 28, battering Kakinada and Visakhapatnam and bringing more than 200 mm of rain to parts of coastal Andhra. As it weakened and moved north-west, it dumped heavy rain on the Eastern Ghats in southern Odisha, where steep terrain and swollen rivers produced the flash floods and landslides of the past two days. Its remnant is now a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh and north-west Odisha.

In Chhattisgarh, where untimely rain is threatening the paddy harvest ahead of procurement beginning on November 15, Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai has ordered district collectors to carry out crop damage surveys and pay relief to eligible farmers, UNI reported.

## What they are saying

"Protecting the lives and property of the state's residents during times of crisis is my utmost priority," Majhi wrote on X after his survey. Chief Secretary Anu Garg said 15 more Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams had been sent because rain was continuing and cloud cover remained low.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has spoken to the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry and said National and State Disaster Response Force teams were working "on a war footing". President Droupadi Murmu telephoned Majhi, and the opposition Biju Janata Dal sent a party delegation to the affected areas.

## What happens next

The India Meteorological Department expects a low-pressure area over the South Andaman Sea to strengthen into a depression over the south-east Bay of Bengal by Saturday, October 31, and move west-north-west towards the Andhra coast over the following two days. It has issued yellow alerts for heavy rain in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri for November 1-3, with an orange alert for Malkangiri on November 2-3. That means more rain for districts that are already flooded.

An inter-ministerial central team is due to visit Odisha on November 2 to assess the damage; central teams have also been sent to Andhra Pradesh.

## Key numbers

Odisha deaths confirmed: 3 (Kandhamal)

Missing in Ganjam: 12 to 13, by different counts

People evacuated in Odisha: about 59,000 across nine districts

Villages flooded in Ganjam and Gajapati: more than 1,000

Andhra Pradesh deaths: 7 (state figure; some reports say 9)

Andhra Pradesh preliminary losses: about Rs 4,600 crore

All casualty, evacuation and damage figures are preliminary.
